---
title: v2.3.0 — Public Work Contracts and Installed CLI Validation
---

## Overview

This release makes the Work Source and Discussion workflows constructible from published contracts. Source capture gains a published request contract; `discussion init` and `recover` derive integrity hashes from a caller-owned draft; and the Discussion result contract documents every response shape. Release package validation now installs the built ZIPs on macOS and Windows, runs the installed Work CLI through public contract, Source, Discussion, and TASK smoke checks, and preserves the results as CI artifacts. Windows installation checks also distinguish cancellation from timeout and manage installer descendants with a Job Object.

## Highlights

- Add the `work-source-capture-request` public contract, bringing the published catalog to 92 contracts, and register its scaffold field order.
- Accept a `DiscussionSessionDraft` for `discussion init` and `discussion recover`: callers supply the semantics and `commit.operation_id`, while `operation_sha256` and `content_sha256` are derived by the CLI from the same canonical rules used for verification.
- Publish the per-command constraints for `work-discussion-result` and give every response shape an example that the Rust response types parse and re-serialize without drift.
- Name `work-source-capture-request` in `invalid_source_metadata` and include its `contract_id`, so a rejected capture points at the contract to inspect.
- Update the Work Skill workflows and README so examples use only flags that exist in `commands.json`, and document that a resumed session is read from saved files rather than from conversation history.
- Cover interrupted and conflicting Discussion recovery, including preserved bytes, revision, and reason codes.
- Validate installed Release ZIPs on macOS and Windows with public contract queries, Source capture, Discussion init/read, and TASK preview/apply/validate; retain CLI output and ZIP version evidence.
- Preserve cancellation as the Windows installer E2E failure reason, report cleanup failures separately, and clean up descendants even when the parent process has exited.
